implantation. Neointimal healing reduces the volume of acute 
stent malapposition with many acute stent malapposition struts 
becoming completely integrated into the vessel wall. How-
ever, cases of acute stent malapposition with a large volume or 
acute stent malapposition located within the edges of the stent 
were not resolved in most cases. Thus, acute stent malapposi-
tion volume and location within stent edges were identified as 
independent predictors of late-persistent stent malapposition. 
Our results indicate that an acute stent malapposition with a 
larger volume or area is more likely to persist at follow-up 
examinations, which is consistent with findings from previous 
studies.4,6,8 Late-persistent stent malapposition could be differ-
entiated from resolved acute stent malapposition by an acute 
stent malapposition area >1.2 mm2 according to an IVUS 
study.6 A strut-to-vessel distance ≤260 µm on poststent OCT 
images was suggested as a cut-off value for resolved acute 
stent malapposition.18 A volume of acute stent malapposition 
>2.56 mm3 best separated late-persistent stent malapposition 
lesions from resolved acute stent malapposition lesions in the 
present study.
